standards.name: COMBINE Archive (OMEX)
standards.abstract: The COMBINE Archive (OMEX) is a packaging format used to bundle computational modeling projects — for example models, simulation experiment descriptions, and associated files — so they can be exchanged, executed, and visualized together. In the provided source material (a runBioSimulations tutorial hosted on TeSS), OMEX is referenced as the target archive format for modeling projects created or executed with runBioSimulations. The tutorial context emphasizes multi-framework/multi-format modeling workflows (e.g., BNGL, SBML) and describes how to create COMBINE/OMEX archives as part of executing and visualizing simulation studies using the runBioSimulations web application and its REST API.

classification.rationale: The source material is prose (a tutorial/description) rather than a specification table or a staged workflow. It contains descriptive guidance and feature statements (sentences) rather than a rows/columns metadata table or a clear ordered sequence of steps, so the content is best represented as principles (prose guidance).

principles.principle: COMBINE/OMEX archives are used to package modeling projects.
principles.evidence: This includes instructions on how to create COMBINE/OMEX archives of modeling projects.

principles.principle: OMEX archives are used in the context of executing and visualizing simulation studies.
principles.evidence: The runBioSimulations tutorial and help describes how to use this web application and web service to execute simulations and visualize their results. This includes instructions on how to create COMBINE/OMEX archives of modeling projects.

principles.principle: OMEX archives can include models and artifacts in a variety of modeling formats (examples: BNGL, SBML).
principles.evidence: runBioSimulations uses BioSimulators to supports a broad range of modeling frameworks (e.g., logical, constraint-based, kinetic), simulation algorithms (e.g., CVODE, FBA, SSA), and modeling formats (e.g., BNGL, SBML).

standards.notes: Source material is a runBioSimulations tutorial page on TeSS (runBioSimulations tutorial and help). The page is authored by Jonathan Karr with contributors listed and primarily describes how to use runBioSimulations and includes instructions for creating COMBINE/OMEX archives; it does not provide a formal OMEX field-level schema or an ordered DAG of steps for archive creation, so extracted items are high-level/principled statements drawn verbatim from the tutorial text.
